This framework will utilize a well-defined state space consisting of sensor signals from specific target gaseous molecules—ammonia (NH3), methane (CH4), and carbon dioxide (CO2)—to enhance the system’s ability to rapidly adapt and distinguish these molecules in real-time.

We propose to develop a hybrid biomimetic olfactory system that integrates a diverse library of advanced semiconductor-based chemiresistors—including p-type oxides, carbon nanotubes, and transition metal dichalcogenides—with a convolutional neural network architecture tailored for feature extraction and pattern recognition. This system will be rigorously tested under varying environmental conditions (specifically at temperatures ranging from 15°C to 35°C and humidity levels from 30% to 80%) to establish its capability in accurately distinguishing and quantifying volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and disease-associated biomarkers at concentrations below current detection limits. Furthermore, we will conduct high-throughput screening of sensor materials, optimizing their performance based on defined metrics of sensitivity, specificity, and operational resilience, and compare our system's performance against conventional electronic nose technologies through controlled benchmarks and real-world applications in environmental monitoring and healthcare diagnostics.

The development of a hybrid biomimetic olfactory system integrating a 5-layer sensor array composed of specific nanostructured metal oxides (e.g., ZnO, TiO2) and PCBM-MAPbI3 heterostructure transistors, utilizing convolutional neural networks for data processing, will enable precise discrimination and quantification of at least six target gaseous molecules, including ammonia (NH3), carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), hydrogen sulfide (H2S), formaldehyde (HCHO), and volatile organic compounds (VOCs). This system will achieve detection limits below 0.5 ppm and a rapid response time of under 100 ms, surpassing conventional electronic noses. Detailed characterization of the materials will involve sol-gel synthesis followed by chemical vapor deposition, with operational parameters set at 25°C and 50% relative humidity. Performance metrics will be benchmarked through controlled experiments against state-of-the-art technologies, establishing a robust framework for real-time, portable olfactory systems applicable to health diagnostics, industrial monitoring, and environmental sensing.
